start.text: The keeper's skiff lies tied to the Heron's back leg, half full of water so still it holds the sky. An oar lies across her thwarts.
Her lantern is in the stern, on its side. Cold. The horn panes are whole, and when you tip it the oil slops inside: full. She didn't run out.
Her painter is made fast to the leg with a neat round turn and two half hitches, snugged down. The way you tie up a boat you mean to come back to.
The little brass bell hangs at her bow again, where it was. It hasn't rung. Nothing out here moves to ring it.
There's a hole worn smooth in her stem-post where the bell hung. It's in your satchel.

bell.text: There's a hole worn smooth in her stem-post, just the size for a loop of tarred cord.

choice.text: Tie the bell back on her bow.

hang.text: You thread the cord through the hole and knot it. The bell hangs at the bow where it hung before. It doesn't ring. Nothing out here moves to ring it.
From the punt, Corran watches you do it, and says nothing, and nods once.

keep.text: You put it away. Somebody carried it half a mile through still water to put it in a trap. You'd like to know who, before it goes back.
It gives one small knock against your ribs as you straighten, and is quiet.
